successCriteria.description: The leave-policy module exposes an ILeavePolicyService interface with exactly five methods — getActivePolicy(leaveTypeId): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>, getPolicyById(id): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>, getAllPolicies(): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>, createPolicy(data: Omit<LeavePolicy,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>): Promise<LeavePolicy>, and updatePolicy(id, data: Partial<LeavePolicy>): Promise<LeavePolicy | null> — each returning the declared type.

A LeavePolicyService class implements ILeavePolicyService and is constructible with an ILeavePolicyRepository injected via its constructor; every method delegates to the corresponding repository method (getActivePolicy→findActiveByLeaveTypeId, getPolicyById→findById, getAllPolicies→findAll, createPolicy→create, updatePolicy→update) passing through the same arguments and returning the repository's result unchanged.

getActivePolicy returns the active (isActive: true) policy for a given leave type id, or null when no active policy exists — observable by asserting the repository's findActiveByLeaveTypeId result is returned verbatim.

createPolicy accepts an input shaped as Omit<LeavePolicy,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'> and returns the persisted LeavePolicy produced by the repository, with no field transformation between the service input and the repository create call.

updatePolicy returns the updated LeavePolicy when the repository finds a matching row, and returns null when the repository reports no match — the null case is propagated, not swallowed or converted to an error.

The barrel index.ts re-exports the service interface (ILeavePolicyService) and service class (LeavePolicyService) alongside the existing model and repository symbols, so downstream modules can import them through the module's public entry point.

Unit tests at tests/unit/modules/leave-policy/leave-policy.service.spec.ts mock ILeavePolicyRepository as a typed object of jest.fn() methods (not the DB pool) and verify each service method invokes the expected repository method with the expected arguments and returns/propagates the mocked result, including the null case and repository-thrown errors.

The service implementation never imports or references the database pool or any SQL — all persistence is reached through the injected ILeavePolicyRepository, satisfying GP-001 (no direct DB access outside the repository layer).

constraints: No `any` types (HARNESS.json no-any rule, severity high): use `unknown` with type guards or precise types; the service interface, implementation, and test mocks must be fully typed with no implicit or explicit `any`.

No direct database access outside the repository (HARNESS.json no-direct-db-outside-repository, severity critical / GP-001): the service must not import the pg pool, connection module, or write SQL; it may only depend on the ILeavePolicyRepository interface.
Strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks) per tsconfig.json — the service must compile under `tsc --noEmit` with the existing strict settings.

Constructor injection of ILeavePolicyRepository is required (settled decision): the service class must accept its repository dependency via the constructor, even though the existing status/uptime services have no constructor because they have no dependencies.

Module-boundary imports: cross-module consumers import leave-policy symbols only through index.ts; within-module files (service.interface.ts, service.ts) may import sibling files by direct relative path, matching the existing status/uptime service convention.
Test file naming uses .spec.ts (leave-policy.service.spec.ts) to stay consistent with the existing leave-policy.repository.spec.ts; jest.config.js testMatch accepts both .test.ts and .spec.ts.
Test mocks must be a typed object of jest.fn() methods matching ILeavePolicyRepository — not a mock of pool.query — because the service depends on the repository interface, not the DB pool.
outOfScope: Controller, routes, and Fastify HTTP surface for leave-policy — this phase creates only the service interface and implementation; the API layer is not in scope.

RBAC enforcement / auth middleware (GP-005) and input validation at API boundaries (GP-003) — these apply at the controller/route layer, which is not built in this phase; the service itself performs no auth checks.
Audit record creation (GP-002) for policy create/update — the service delegates directly to the repository and does not write audit records; audit wiring is deferred to the orchestration phases.

Business-rule enforcement beyond delegation — the service does not validate "at most one active policy per leaveTypeId", entitlement ranges, or notice-day constraints; such validation belongs to later orchestration/controller phases.
The LeaveBalance service, Notification service, LeaveRequest service, and business-day utility — these are Phases 9 and 10 and are not part of the leave-policy service layer.
Integration/e2e tests against a real database — this phase ships only Jest unit tests with a mocked repository.

entityInvariants.invariant: At most one active policy exists per leaveTypeId (ARCHITECTURE.md / reconciled.json key rule). The service's getActivePolicy must surface this constraint by returning a single active policy or null — it must never return an array or silently pick among multiple active rows; the repository's findActiveByLeaveTypeId (which filters WHERE is_active = true and returns the first row) is the authoritative source.

id, createdAt, and updatedAt are system-managed and never supplied by callers: createPolicy's input is Omit<LeavePolicy,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>, and updatePolicy must not allow callers to overwrite id or createdAt (the repository already strips read-only fields; the service must not re-introduce them).

The service contract is a pure delegation layer over ILeavePolicyRepository: each method maps one-to-one to a repository method with no additional persistence, no cross-module calls, and no business-rule side effects — it must remain substitutable by any ILeavePolicyRepository-backed implementation.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at the service layer (RBAC is deferred to the controller/middleware phase); the service performs no role checks.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only and idempotent; returns null when no active policy exists for the leave type; propagates repository errors unchanged without catching or wrapping.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at the service layer.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only and idempotent; returns null when no policy matches the id; propagates repository errors unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at the service layer.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only and idempotent; returns an empty array (never null) when no policies exist; propagates repository errors unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at the service layer; GP-002 audit recording is deferred to orchestration phases, so this method does not itself write an audit record.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Not idempotent (each call persists a new row); propagates repository errors — including unique-constraint violations on (leave_type_id, is_active) — unchanged without catching or wrapping; returns the persisted LeavePolicy.

interfaceConstraints.operation: updatePolicy(id: string, data: Partial<LeavePolicy>): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at the service layer; GP-002 audit recording is deferred to orchestration phases.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Idempotent for no-op updates (returns the existing row when no mutable fields are supplied); returns null when no row matches the id (the null is propagated, not converted to a thrown error); propagates repository errors unchanged.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The ILeavePolicyService method signatures must align one-to-one with ILeavePolicyRepository: getActivePolicy→findActiveByLeaveTypeId(leaveTypeId): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>, getPolicyById→findById(id): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>, getAllPolicies→findAll(): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>, createPolicy→create(policy: Omit<LeavePolicy,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>): Promise<LeavePolicy>, updatePolicy→update(id, data: Partial<LeavePolicy>): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>. The createPolicy input type must be exactly Omit<LeavePolicy,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'> so it passes through to repo.create with no transformation.

The service interface and implementation must import and use the canonical LeavePolicy interface from leave-policy.model.ts (id, policyName, leaveTypeId, entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt) — no redefinition or drift of the entity shape.

The barrel must continue to export the existing model and repository symbols (LeaveType, LeavePolicy, ILeavePolicyRepository, LeavePolicyRepository) and additionally export ILeavePolicyService and LeavePolicyService, matching the re-export pattern used by src/modules/status/index.ts and src/modules/uptime/index.ts (model, service interface, service class).

The service interface file must follow the established convention: the interface file imports the model type and exports an I<Name>Service interface, and the implementation file imports the interface plus the model and declares a class that implements it — mirroring status.service.interface.ts / status.service.ts and uptime.service.interface.ts / uptime.service.ts.

The service spec must mirror the existing leave-policy.repository.spec.ts structure and location (tests/unit/modules/leave-policy/, .spec.ts extension, ts-jest preset) and use the same makeRow-style fixture pattern adapted for LeavePolicy objects, so the two leave-policy test files are stylistically consistent.

integrationPoints.why: The service's sole dependency: constructor-injected and the only path to persistence. Every service method delegates to a repository method; the service has no other data source.

Downstream phases (Phase 9 LeaveBalanceService.initializeBalance looks up the active policy via ILeavePolicyService, and Phase 10 LeaveRequestService uses ILeavePolicyService) must import the service through the barrel, per the module-boundary import rule.
The new leave-policy.service.spec.ts must be discovered by the existing testMatch glob (**/tests/**/*.spec.(ts|js)) and compile under ts-jest with strict TypeScript.
